subject.title: fix: restore GitHub Copilot turns and account context limits

question: After refreshing onto current main, should the shared credential-rematerialization changes and the legacy JSON-to-SQLite Copilot token-cache migration land together as the fix for the linked runtime bug?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and well-proven, but it crosses shared auth-provider and availability-critical runtime boundaries and changes persisted credential-cache behavior; repository policy and the protected label require a human to accept that combined merge surface.

options.title: Refresh, validate, and land together
options.body: Rebase or merge current main, rerun exact-head auth/runtime and cache-upgrade proof, then merge the cohesive fix if the reviewed merge result remains clean.

options.title: Split the cache migration
options.body: Land the runtime transport and metadata fix separately while moving the bounded SQLite cache migration into a narrower follow-up with dedicated upgrade proof.

options.title: Pause the combined change
options.body: Keep the PR open until an owner can reduce or explicitly accept the shared-runtime and persisted-cache blast radius.

recommendation.title: Refresh, validate, and land together
recommendation.body: Rebase or merge current main, rerun exact-head auth/runtime and cache-upgrade proof, then merge the cohesive fix if the reviewed merge result remains clean.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged both foundational GitHub Copilot changes and are the strongest history-backed owner for accepting the combined shared-runtime and cache-migration risk.
